reviewMethod: Complete line-by-line semantic review of the platform feature-flag definitions, cookie/session and platform configuration, platform context types, product registry and permanent platform-core policy, including malformed environment values, production cookie transport, bounded access-session lifetime, single-timestamp JWT issuance, product-to-flag derivation, permission metadata and the distinction between availability flags and security or launch gates.

residualRisks.statement: This bounded slice reviews five platform-core authority paths only; the remaining Batch 1 deployment, package, changelog and script paths retain their pending status and no repository-wide completion claim is made.

The product registry and feature flags currently provide metadata and helper-level availability decisions but are not imported as universal route launch gates; authorization and domain-specific release gates remain independently mandatory.

TypeScript aliases and unions cannot validate tenant, workspace, role or product values read from PostgreSQL; the runtime adapters and tenant-principal authority retain their assigned Batch 2 and Batch 3 semantic reviews.

The unified-session signer is changed only to bind issued-at and expiry to one timestamp and is structurally covered by this policy; its complete authentication semantics remain pending the assigned Batch 3 review.

reviewNotes: Input validation, exact source contracts, ordering-sensitive production cookie enforcement, single-timestamp JWT checks, platform type requirements, product identity coverage and duplicate callback rejection were reviewed line by line.
The policy deliberately consumes the pending unified-session source only for the bounded timestamp remediation and does not mark that Batch 3 file semantically reviewed.
All five flag identifiers, environment mappings, absent-value defaults, exact configured values and aggregate snapshot behavior were reviewed against every repository consumer.
The module now states that availability flags are not authorization or release gates and treats every configured value other than exact true or false as disabled.

findings.attackPath: A malformed configured value such as FEATURE_EXCHANGE_ENABLED=TRUE or FEATURE_MENTOR_ENABLED=1 formerly fell through to defaultEnabled; for default-on products, an operator typo intended to control availability left the product reported and evaluated as enabled.
findings.affectedInvariant: An explicitly configured but unrecognized availability value must never inherit an enabled default.
findings.evidence: The former final branch returned config.defaultEnabled for every value except exact true and false; academy, exchange and mentor all have enabled defaults.
findings.verificationRequirement: The permanent platform-core test must prove absent values retain documented defaults while malformed configured values fail closed for a default-on flag.

reviewNotes: Every current and legacy cookie name, Secure inference branch, duration parser, minimum and maximum access lifetime and platform metadata constant were reviewed against production validation and session consumers.
Production now returns Secure before reading any insecure override, and the relative JWT duration-string helper was removed so access-token timestamps use the numeric lifetime authority.

findings.attackPath: TECPEY_COOKIE_SECURE=false formerly returned before production or canonical HTTPS inference, allowing a production misconfiguration to issue session, refresh, WebAuthn, 2FA, password-rotation and Academy cookies without the Secure transport attribute.
findings.affectedInvariant: Authentication cookies issued by a production process must always carry Secure regardless of a weakening environment override.
findings.evidence: The helper is shared by all listed authentication issuers; the former explicit false branch preceded URL inference and validate-env did not reject TECPEY_COOKIE_SECURE=false.
findings.verificationRequirement: Runtime and structural tests must prove NODE_ENV=production returns true even with an explicit false override and an HTTP loopback site URL.

findings.attackPath: The former sessionMaxAge relative-duration string was applied by jose after setIssuedAt had already read the wall clock; crossing a one-second boundary between those calls produced a JWT lifetime of 14,401 seconds despite the declared 14,400-second ceiling.
findings.affectedInvariant: An access credential must not outlive its governed four-hour maximum or the browser cookie lifetime by even a scheduler-boundary second.
findings.evidence: Full Suite Diagnostics on exact head d6c406e8 observed exp minus iat equal to 14,401 while configured and cookie lifetimes were 14,400; jose resolves the two relative claims using separate Date reads.
findings.verificationRequirement: The signer must compute one integer issuedAt value and set exp to issuedAt plus sessionMaxAgeSeconds; focused tests and the permanent policy must reject the former relative-duration API.

reviewNotes: Identity aliases, all seven roles, six product IDs, plan names, tenant and workspace records, membership lifecycle fields and request-time PlatformContext were reviewed in full.
The declarations accurately model compile-time consumers; runtime validation of database strings is explicitly retained as cross-batch residual risk rather than implied by these types.

Product IDs, slugs, names, descriptions, typed access permissions, flag mappings, always-available knowledge behavior and lookup/filter helpers were reviewed against platform types and feature configuration.

The registry is now immutable at its public boundary and derives each isEnabled callback from the same declared featureFlag, eliminating the former duplicate string assignment as a future drift surface.
